item.title: UK Food Prices to Peak Lower Than Thought, BOE Survey Finds
item.description: Britain’s supermarkets plan to raise food prices by less than previously thought as rising fuel costs caused by the Middle East conflict dents household demand, the Bank of England’s survey of regional business contacts said.

item.title: Mauritius Tax Wave Threatens to Erode Its Banks’ Profitability
item.description: A raft of new corporate taxes that could erode banks’ profitability is testing Mauritius’s long-standing status as a low-tax gateway for cross-border capital, according to Moody’s Ratings.

item.title: PIC: Why South Africa’s Biggest Fund Manager Is in Turmoil
item.description: The South African firm that oversees state workers’ pensions has been plunged into a fresh crisis triggered by the suspension of its chief executive and the resignation of its chairman.

item.title: SoftBank Weighs Deal for Robotics Startup Gravis
item.description: SoftBank Group Corp. is considering an acquisition of Gravis Robotics AG, people familiar with the matter said, as the Japanese investor targets the artificial intelligence technologies underpinning robotics.

item.title: ECB Starts Onboarding Process for Enhanced Repo Facility
item.description: The European Central Bank started the onboarding process for non-euro area central banks to allow them to tap euro liquidity later this year.

item.title: Victoria Plc Slumps to £326 Million Loss as Debt Deal Bites
item.description: Victoria Plc reported a wider annual loss as the troubled British carpetmaker counted the cost of its recent debt refinancing.

item.title: UK Economy Boosted by World Cup and Sunshine, PMI Shows
item.description: The World Cup, staycations and scorching weather helped Britain’s private sector bounce back in July, though mounting tensions in the Middle East threatened to scupper the nascent rebound.

item.title: Zara’s Ortega Buys Paris Office Complex for About €800 Million
item.description: Zara billionaire Amancio Ortega bought a business center in Paris from Invesco Ltd., in what is his biggest transaction in Europe.

item.title: How Franchise Restaurants Opened the Door to the Gig Economy
item.description: The ruthless labor history of your favorite fast food joint.

item.title: Odd Lots: How Franchising Led to the Gig Economy (Podcast)
item.description: When the fast food industry began booming in the 1950s, it did so via a new business model known as the franchise. This model allowed independent operators to license trademarks from a business like McDonald’s or Dunkin Donuts, and it soon spread across the country, with huge consequences for how Americans are employed. item.title: Euro-Zone Business Activity Jumps to Five-Month High
item.description: Euro-area private-sector activity improved much more than expected in July, returning to pre-Iran-war levels, though the most recent escalation of the conflict threatens to weigh on sentiment once again.

item.title: ECB Says Consumer Price Expectations Fell Sharply in June
item.description: Inflation expectations among euro-area consumers for the next year declined significantly in June, a period that predates the oil spike triggered by a new flareup in fighting in the Middle East.

item.title: ECB Officials Avoid Clear Hints on Possible Hike for Now
item.description: European Central Bank policymakers shirked from signaling a potential hike in borrowing costs in September, waiting for data to justify any move.

item.title: Bain and LY Are Said to Mull Higher Bid for Kakaku, Rivaling EQT
item.description: Bain Capital and LY Corp. are considering making a fresh joint offer for Japanese online marketplace Kakaku.com Inc., people familiar with the matter said, marking an escalation in the bidding war with private equity firm EQT AB.

item.title: Vietnam Weighs Limiting Social Media Use for Children Under 16
item.description: Vietnam may ban children under 16 years old from posting, commenting or reacting to posts on social media as the country looks to join other governments tightening online protections for minors.

item.title: Khazanah Is Said to Sell $340 Million Tenaga Stake in Placement
item.description: Malaysian sovereign wealth fund Khazanah Nasional Bhd. has sold 1.39 billion ringgit ($340 million) worth of shares in state-owned power firm Tenaga Nasional Bhd., according to people with knowledge of the matter.

item.title: Chinese Banks Break With Lending Benchmark in Pricing New Credit
item.description: Three of the biggest Chinese banks experimented with anchoring new loans to interbank rates, a step toward a new pricing mechanism that could better reflect supply and demand for money in the market.

item.title: Malaysia May Again Host Formula One Racing as Iran War Puts Bahrain in Doubt
item.description: Malaysia could host a Formula One race for the first time in nine years, potentially replacing the Bahrain Grand Prix as the Middle East conflict drags on, according to the country’s Youth and Sports Minister Mohammed Taufiq Johari.

item.title: German Private-Sector Activity Unexpectedly Returns to Growth
item.description: German business activity unexpectedly expanded for the first time since March, though the latest escalation in the Middle East could yet derail the euro zone’s top economy.

item.title: South Africa Seeks Private Capital to Tackle Water Crisis
item.description: South Africa plans to tap private investors to tackle the country’s water crisis by developing blended-finance projects and accelerating a pipeline of bankable infrastructure investments.

item.title: French Private-Sector Activity at Highest Level Since February
item.description: Private-sector activity in France contracted only marginally this month, though renewed hostilities in the Middle East cloud the outlook for the euro area’s second-biggest economy.

item.title: Japan Banks With Shipping Finance Expertise Are Latest to Merge
item.description: A proposed merger between Iyogin Holdings Inc. and Ehime Bank Ltd. adds to a series of recent M&A activity between Japanese regional lenders as an aging and shrinking population weighs on their business.

item.title: India’s Biggest IPO of 2026 Briefly Dips Below Offer Price
item.description: SBI Funds Management Ltd.’s shares briefly fell below their offer price just four days after their trading debut, signaling weak secondary-market demand for the nation’s largest asset manager.

item.title: Traders Look to Politburo for Cues on China’s Growth Commitment
item.description: China’s Politburo meeting later this month will test Beijing’s commitment to supporting growth, with investors expecting targeted measures to bolster stability rather than a sweeping stimulus package.

item.title: Japanese Shoppers Are Driving Up Jewelry Sales to a Record
item.description: Japanese shoppers are driving up luxury jewelry sales to a record as consumers seek a safe haven from inflation and the weakening yen.

item.title: Japan’s 40-Year Yield Rises 10 Basis Points on Inflation Fears
item.description: Japan’s 40-year government bond yield rose 10 basis points, as investors remain unconvinced that the nation’s central bank will tighten policy fast enough to quell inflation.

item.title: Tech Stocks Face Investor Skepticism as Rally Stalls and Profit Estimates Rise
item.description: The earnings season is confirming worries that the technology rally had gone too far, with investors now harder to please and reluctant to buy into rising profit estimates.

item.title: UK Retail Sales Beat Forecasts Again With Strong June Increase
item.description: UK retail sales defied expectations again with a surprisingly strong rise in June, as sunny weather and the World Cup outweighed any concern among shoppers over the cost of living.

item.title: Tanker Exits Red Sea Dark as Another China Ship Heads to Strait
item.description: A Greek tanker carrying Saudi crude exited the Red Sea with its transponder off, while another Chinese vessel headed toward Bab el-Mandeb as Houthi attacks heightened risks for commercial shipping.
